title: What does the XRPL AccountTxnID account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of AccountTxnID and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, AccountTxnID makes the account track its most recent transaction hash for transaction chaining. [1]

It is an opt-in account property rather than an ordinary permission to transfer funds. The common AccountTxnID field can bind a transaction to an expected predecessor. A Ticket-based transaction cannot combine that mechanism in the same way. Treat a stale predecessor as a reason to reconcile account history rather than guessing a replacement hash. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for AccountTxnID and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why AccountTxnID is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
